title: Commit hook resolves the approval trust map from the repo when the env var is unset

outcomes.statement: A commit succeeds without the operator exporting WORK_READINESS_APPROVAL_KEYS_JSON by hand, because the hook resolves the committed public-key map itself.
outcomes.demo: With the variable unset, git commit passes the readiness gate; with a corrupt .work-readiness-trust.json and the variable unset, it still fails closed.

uncertainties.statement: Whether resolving trust from a repository file weakens the gate, since a pushed commit could add an attacker's public key alongside the signature it validates.
uncertainties.resolution: It would weaken CI, so the fallback is confined to .githooks/commit-msg, which git never runs in CI. CI and the range gate keep reading only WORK_READINESS_APPROVAL_KEYS_JSON and still fail closed when it is absent (WORK_READINESS.md:119-126, still tracked as CHG-027). Locally the fallback grants nothing new: an operator who can edit the trust file can already export any value they like, so the trust boundary is unchanged on a machine its owner controls.

uncertainties.statement: Whether the fallback could mask a genuinely missing or malformed trust map.
uncertainties.resolution: The hook only sets the variable when it is unset AND the file exists; it never overrides an explicitly exported value, and it does not validate the contents. model.mjs still rejects missing, malformed, unknown, or non-Ed25519 trust, so a corrupt file fails closed exactly as before.
